Author: Rajeev Misra

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Court No. - 49
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 20697 of 2023
Applicant :- Rameshwar Singh Yadav
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Syed Imran Ibrahim,Praveen Kumar Singh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
1. Heard Mr. Syed Imran Ibrahim, the learned counsel for applicant and Mr. Rajesh Mishra, the learned A.G.A. for State.

2. Perused the record.
3.

This application for bail has been filed by applicant-Rameshwar Singh Yadav seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 103 of 2022, under Sections 447, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(va) SC/ST (P.A.) Act, Police Station-Malawan, District-Etah during the pendency of trial.

Rameshwar Singh Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67916739/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Record shows that in respect of an incident which is alleged to have occurred on 02.06.2021, a belated FIR dated 17.06.2022 was lodged by first informant-Geetam Singh and was registered as Case Crime No. Case Crime No. 103 of 2022, under Sections 447, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(va) SC/ST (P.A.) Act, Police Station-Malawan, District-Etah.

entities.text: Case Crime No. Case Crime No. 103 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: In the aforesaid FIR, 3 persons namely (1) Rameshwar Singh Yadav, (2) Jugendra Singh Yadav and (3) Subodh Kumar have been nominated as named accused whereas an unknown person also been arraigned as accused.

5. The gravamen of the allegations made in the FIR is to the affect that named accused have illegally and forcibly occupied the land of the first informant i.e. Survey Plot No. 565/2, area 0.761 Hectare.
6. Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is innocent.
He has falsely implicated in aforementioned case crime number.
Allegations made in the FIR are false and concocted.

As such,
applicant is being falsely prosecuted in aforementioned case crime number.

7. He has then invited the attention of Court to the document occurring at page 94 of the paper book and on basis thereof, he contends that in respect of the land in dispute, proceedings under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act were held.

However, compensation was denied to the first informant primarily on the ground that since father of the first informant has already executed a lease of 99 years in favour of the wife of present applicant, therefore, he is not entitled to compensation.
The copy of the lease deed has been brought on record as Annexure-11 to the affidavit filed in support of present application.

8. On the above premise, the learned counsel for applicant submits that prima-facie the allegations made in the FIR are contrary to the documents on record which cannot disputed as the same fall in the realm of public documents.
9. It is then contended that there is a delay of almost 1 year in lodging the FIR.
However, neither in the FIR nor in the statement of first informant recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., there is any explanation regarding the delay in lodging the FIR.
He, therefore, submits that once the delay in lodging the FIR remains un-explained, the prosecution of the applicant itself cannot be maintained.
In support of above, reliance is placed upon the judgment of Supreme Court in P. Rajagopal And Ors. Vs. The State of Tamil Nadu, AIR 2019 SC 2866/2019(5) SCC 403 (paragraph 8).

entities.text: P. Rajagopal And Ors. Vs. The State of Tamil Nadu, AIR 2019 SC 2866/2019(5) SCC 403 (paragraph 8).
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. He further submits that though applicant has criminal history but the same has been duly explained in paragraph 2 of the supplementary affidavit filed in Court today.

On the above premise,
it is thus urged that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.

In case, applicant is enlarged on bail,
he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
The charge sheet has already been submitted, therefore, evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant now stand crystallized.
There is nothing on record to show that the custodial arrest of applicant is absolutely necessary during the course of trial.
On the above premise, the learned counsel for applicant contends that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case, applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.

entities.text: Rameshwar Singh Yadav vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
However, he could not dislodge the factual/legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant with reference to the record at this stage.

12. Having heard, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and upon perusal of material brought on record as well as the complicity of applicant and accusation made coupled with the fact that father of informant has himself executed a lease of 99 years as is explicit from the document occurring as Annexure-11 to the affidavit, the denial of compensation to the first informant, on the above ground as is manifest from the document occurring at page 94 of the paper book, the criminal antecedents of the applicants having been duly explained in paragraph 2 of the supplementary affidavit, the charge sheet having been submitted, therefore, the evidence sought to be relied upon by the proseuction against applicant now stand crystallized, there is no such circumstance necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during course of trial, but without making any comment on the merits of the case, applicant has made out a case for bail.
13. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant-Rameshwar Singh Yadav, be released on bail in aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) THE APPLICANT SHALL FILE AN UNDERTAKING TO THE EFFECT THAT HE/SHE SHALL NOT SEEK ANY ADJOURNMENT ON THE DATE FIXED FOR EVIDENCE WHEN THE WITNESSES ARE PRESENT IN COURT.
IN CASE OF DEFAULT OF THIS CONDITION, IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT IT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PASS ORDERS IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(ii) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON EACH DATE FIXED, EITHER PERSONALLY OR THROUGH HIS/HER COUNSEL.
IN CASE OF HIS/HER ABSENCE, WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THE TRIAL COURT MAY PROCEED AGAINST HIM/HER UNDER SECTION 229-A IPC.

(iii) IN CASE, THE APPLICANT MISUSES THE LIBERTY OF BAIL DURING TRIAL AND IN ORDER TO SECURE HIS/HER PRESENCE PROCLAMATION UNDER SECTION 82 CR.P.C., MAY BE ISSUED AND IF APPLICANT FAILS TO APPEAR BEFORE THE COURT ON THE DATE FIXED IN SUCH PROCLAMATION, THEN,
THE TRIAL COURT SHALL INITIATE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST HIM/HER, IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW, UNDER SECTION 174-A IPC.

(iv) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT, IN PERSON, BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON DATES FIXED FOR (1) OPENING OF THE CASE, (2) FRAMING OF CHARGE AND (3) RECORDING OF STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 313 Rameshwar Singh Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67916739/
3 CR.P.C. IF IN THE OPINION OF THE TRIAL COURT ABSENCE OF THE APPLICANT IS DELIBERATE OR WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THEN IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT SUCH DEFAULT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PROCEED AGAINST THE HIM/HER IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.

entities.text: Rameshwar Singh Yadav vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(v) THE TRIAL COURT MAY MAKE ALL POSSIBLE EFFORTS/ENDEAVOUR AND TRY TO CONCLUDE THE TRIAL WITHIN A PERIOD OF ONE YEAR AFTER THE RELEASE OF THE APPLICANT.
15.

However, it is made clear that any wilful violation of above conditions by the applicant, shall have serious repercussion on his bail so granted by this Court and the trial court is at liberty to cancel the bail, after recording the reasons for doing so, in the given case of any of the condition mentioned above.
